market_context.summary: Online accounted for 29.3% of UK retail sales in October 2026 (ONS), with a seasonal peak of 32.5% in November 2025. Amazon.co.uk has by far the largest audience (about 156 million UK web visits in October 2026, Semrush), followed by eBay, and grocery is led online by Tesco, which reports an online market share of 36.7% (excluding rapid delivery) and £3.7 billion of UK online sales in the first half of 2026/27. In beauty and personal care, Mintel's 2026 report says Boots 'reinforces [its] market leading position' online, that supermarkets are the key destination for online purchases and that 77% of adults bought the category online in the past year. TikTok Shop describes itself as the UK's fourth-largest beauty retailer after 60% growth in 2025, while dedicated rapid-delivery firms Getir and Gorillas left the market in 2024 and quick commerce now runs through grocers and aggregators such as Deliveroo (owned by DoorDash since October 2025). The nine mass-market products sampled were stocked across Boots, Superdrug, Tesco, Sainsbury's, Asda, Morrisons and Amazon.

key_facts.fact: Internet sales were 29.3% of total UK retail sales in October 2026 (28.6% in September 2026; 32.5% in November 2025), ONS series J4MC released 20 November 2026.

Worldpanel by Numerator grocery market shares for the 12 weeks to 1 November 2026: Tesco 27.8%, Sainsbury's 15.5%, Asda 11.3%, Aldi 10.4%, Lidl 8.6%, Morrisons 8.3%, Ocado 2.3% (a record; sales £822 million, +12%). Consumer-panel estimate reported by news services, not a regulator statistic.
key_facts.source_name: Worldpanel by Numerator via AJ Bell / Alliance News and Shopappy

key_facts.fact: Mintel's 'UK Online Beauty and Personal Care Retailing Market Report 2026' states that Boots 'reinforces [its] market leading position', that 'supermarkets are the key destination for online BPC purchases' and that 77% of adults bought beauty and personal care online in the past year; the underlying share figures are paywalled (Not publicly disclosed).

Tesco reported UK online sales of £3.7 billion for the 26 weeks to 29 August 2026 (+8.4%); its interim statement says 'our online market share (which excludes rapid delivery) grew +16bps to 36.7%'. This is a company-stated share, not a regulator figure.
Boots (year to 31 August 2025): total revenue £7.54 billion, retail revenue £5.26 billion, Boots.com revenue +18.3%, about 17 million Advantage Card members, 1,824 stores.
key_facts.source_name: Boots accounts as reported by Pharmacy Magazine

key_facts.fact: TikTok Shop says it is the UK's fourth-largest beauty retailer, with beauty sales up 60% year on year in 2025 (company claim; the ranking source is not named in the article). A July 2026 report cited in a search-result summary instead calls it the second-largest, which could not be verified.

IGD says pure-play rapid-delivery operators Getir and Gorillas exited the UK in 2024 and forecasts UK quick commerce to grow 10.7% a year from 2026 to 2031, reaching £5.5 billion and 15% of online grocery; it puts Sainsbury's quick-commerce sales above £700 million in 2025 (+69%) and Tesco Whoosh above £400 million (+51%).

Semrush's October 2026 list of most-visited UK retail websites is led by amazon.co.uk (156.43 million UK visits), ebay.co.uk (69.22 million), argos.co.uk (38.96 million), etsy.com, asda.com (26.27 million), boots.com (24.87 million), temu.com (23.47 million) and tesco.com (21.13 million).

ranking_method_note: Scores follow the brief's rubric exactly: five criteria scored 1-5, weighted 0.20 / 0.25 / 0.20 / 0.15 / 0.20, summed and rounded to two decimals; rank 1 is the highest weighted score. Ties are broken by beauty_category_relevance, then consumer_reach; where a tie still remained, brand_competitor_coverage, data_integration_feasibility, ecommerce_significance and finally alphabetical order were used (an addition, because the rubric is silent). estimated_market_importance reflects overall importance in the country's online retail (tier_1 = market-shaping, tier_2 = significant, tier_3 = niche or emerging), not category relevance, which is captured separately in beauty_relevance. Scoring anchors: ecommerce_significance 5 = market-shaping leader, 4 = top-tier national player, 3 = significant category or regional player, 2 = niche or emerging. consumer_reach uses Semrush estimates of UK web visits for October 2026 (5 = 100 million or more, 4 = 20-100 million, 3 = 5-20 million, 2 = 1-5 million, 1 = below 1 million), adjusted where company-reported customer metrics justify it; web visits exclude app use, which understates grocers and delivery apps. brand_competitor_coverage is an evidence-graded judgement. Checklist used for the UK (nine products sampled on the price-comparison site Trolley.co.uk on 2026-11-26): Dove body wash, Pantene shampoo, Head & Shoulders shampoo, Garnier Ultimate Blends shampoo, Sensodyne toothpaste, Nivea Creme, Vaseline body lotion, L'Oréal Elvive shampoo and Colgate Total toothpaste. A retailer stocking six or more of the nine scores 5 and five scores 4; platforms that could not be checked receive a neutral 3 (or 2 where positioning points to low coverage) and are marked UNVERIFIED. data_integration_feasibility: 5 = documented public partner API plus accessible public pages, 4 = documented API with gated scope, 3 = no API but public pages or sitemaps accessible, 2 = no API and bot-protected pages. The formula rewards reach and data access; Boots ranks below Amazon for that reason even though Mintel names Boots the online market leader for the category, and Sainsbury's ranks below smaller grocers because its site is closed to automated access. These reservations are recorded in the relevant priority_rationale fields.
